about: A rewrite of the diff and cmp tools in Rust, aiming to work the same as GNU diffutils.

prs.title: cmp takes sizes like 1K for how many bytes to compare
prs.broken: Telling cmp to compare only the first 1K or 2M of two files failed with an invalid value error. It only took a plain number, while GNU cmp takes sizes with units.
prs.changed: The byte limit now reads the same unit sizes as the option for skipping bytes at the start.
prs.matters: Scripts that limit cmp with sizes like 1K work the same as with GNU cmp.

prs.title: Context diffs now mark whole changed blocks
prs.broken: When a block of lines was replaced by a block of a different length, the context format marked only some lines as changed and showed the rest as plain deletions or additions. GNU diff marks the whole block.
prs.changed: Every line in a changed block now gets the change mark, as in GNU diff.
prs.matters: Context diffs match GNU's output, so tools that read them see one change, not a split one.

prs.title: One-line adds and deletes print as a single number
prs.broken: diff wrote a single added line as "1a2,2" where GNU diff writes "1a2". Deletes and the ed format had the same problem.
prs.changed: One-line ranges are now written as one number, the same as GNU diff.
prs.matters: Tools and tests that compare against GNU diff output get the same text.

prs.title: cmp lines up its byte offsets after skipped bytes
prs.broken: With bytes skipped at the start, cmp -l padded each offset as if nothing had been skipped, so the columns came out wider than GNU cmp's.
prs.changed: The column width now comes from the bytes actually left to compare, after the skips.
prs.matters: Scripts that read cmp -l output get the same text as with GNU cmp.
